title: Relay-run ledger follow-ups from v1.16
lead: The relay board draws a waiting step with its own marker instead of a spinner. `relay-run list` shows how long a step has waited, and step JSON carries `waiting_since`. `counts.roles` counts the role steps under the orchestrator, `ui` included. Snapshot runs carry each step's `waiting_on` and latest `question`. The relay contract and `docs/commands.md` say that a heartbeat ends a wait and that an answer may span lines. All of this is pinned by tests.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** any new wire field or event in the ledger, relay-run stats (s408), a gate verdict, a contract version bump (s424 bundles v1.17's rule changes into v11), a `--text-file` input for answers, and the TUI's `[ ] ROLE waiting` label for a role that has not begun.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
These are the review findings left as later during the v1.16 relay (s404, s392, s396, s399). Checked against the code on 2026-10-30:

- `tui._marker` returns the spinner for any step that is not done or failed in an active run, so a `wait` step spins as if it were working (s404).
- The fold keeps no wait start. `Step.updated_at` moves on every event, so neither `relay-run list` nor the board can say how long a step has waited (s404). `docs/commands.md` (Waiting on the owner) already says a later `--phase start` ends a wait. The contract's heartbeat sentences do not: `src/slicer/ai.py`, the relay-run paragraph of `ai relay` and the orchestrator's "Relay run" rule. An orchestrator that heartbeats a waiting step silently ends its wait.
- `Run.counts` counts `roles` only for steps with no parent. The contract records every role round with `--parent` set to the orchestrator's step, so for every contract-shaped run `counts.roles` is `{"orchestrator": 1}`, which this repo's 15 runs confirm. The bug is not specific to `ui` (s392). ork's `internal/slicercli/types.go` parses `counts.roles` but nothing in ork reads it.
- `snapshot.build`'s `runs()` keeps only `id, role, phase, task, model` per step, so a dashboard sees `wait` but not what the step waits on or which question is open (s396).
- `relay-run answer --text` already accepts multi-line text. `ops.relay_run_answer` only strips it, `test_Answer_Text_RecordsFreeTextWithNoOption` records `"Neither.\nUse sqlite."`, and `--why` is the same. What is missing is a doc line and a test that `--get` prints every line (s396).
- The spec-check question is settled. `ai relay` says the outer session records the spec check's round with `--role spec-check` and no `--parent`, in a run it begins on the batch, and ends that run. The orchestrator never runs the spec check, so its brief has nothing to say. `tests/test_ai.py::test_Relay_UiPassAndSpecCheckNameTheirLedgerRoles` pins the text. This bullet needs no change (s399).

Owner decisions:

- (default accepted by the owner 2026-10-30) A waiting step draws `[?]` in the `parked` style role (owner question 7).
- (default accepted by the owner 2026-10-30) `counts.roles` counts lane steps, using the TUI's rule (owner question 6).
- (default accepted by the owner 2026-10-30) The heartbeat sentence goes into the contract text now, with no version bump, and s424's v11 `RELAY_CHANGES` entry names it (owner question 8).
- (default accepted by the owner 2026-10-30) A multi-line answer needs only the doc line and a test (owner question 9).
- (default accepted by the owner 2026-10-30) A snapshot step's `question` is the same object `relay-run list` gives, and `snapshot` stays version 1 because the keys are additive (owner question 10).

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/relayrun.py`:
  - `Step` gains `waiting_since: str = ""`. `_apply` sets it to the event's `at` when the step enters `wait` or changes what it waits on, keeps it across repeated wait events, and clears it when the wait ends. `to_dict` puts it after `waiting_on`, and `from_dict` reads it with `.get(..., "")`.
  - `Run.in_lane(step) -> bool` is moved from the predicate in `tui._lane`: no parent, or the parent's role is `orchestrator`. `Run.counts` counts `roles` over lane steps.
  - `elapsed_text` moves here from `tui.py`, so `cli` can use it without importing `tui`.
- `src/slicer/tui.py`:
  - `_marker` returns `("?", "parked")` for `step.phase == "wait"` in an active run, at every tick.
  - `_lane` uses `Run.in_lane`.
  - A waiting step's row (and the orchestrator row) carries a `wait:WAITING_ON` cell and `waited Xm` from `waiting_since` to `now`.
  - `elapsed_text` is imported from `relayrun`.
- `src/slicer/cli.py`: `_step_line` appends the time waited after `wait:WAITING_ON`, as of `relayrun.utcnow()`.
- `src/slicer/snapshot.py`: in `runs()`, each step adds `waiting_on` and `question` (`step.question.to_dict()` or `None`) after its current keys.
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: the heartbeat sentence in the `ai relay` relay-run paragraph and in the orchestrator's "Relay run" rule gains: "A heartbeat on a waiting step ends its wait: do not heartbeat a step that waits." Regenerate `tests/fixtures/relay-contract-v10.json` if it changes.
- Tests: `tests/test_relay_run.py`, `tests/test_tui.py` (`RelayBoardLinesTests`, which uses `board_step` and `board_run`), `tests/test_snapshot.py`, `tests/test_ai.py`.
- Docs:
  - `docs/commands.md`: the `relay-run list` and `relay-run answer` rows, and Waiting on the owner.
  - `docs/agents.md`: the `relay-run list` row (`waiting_since`, the new `counts.roles` meaning) and Dashboard snapshot (`runs` step keys).
  - `docs/tui.md`: the `[?]` marker, beside `[|]`, `[+]`, `[!]` and `[~]`.
  - `CHANGELOG.md` under Changed.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- `test_BoardLines_WaitingStep_ShowsWaitMarkerAtEveryTick`: a reviewer step in phase `wait` (`waiting_on` `owner`) in an active run shows `[?]` on its row for ticks 0 to 4, never a spinner frame. Its row role is `parked`, and the row carries `wait:owner`.
- `test_BoardLines_WaitingOrchestrator_ShowsWaitMarkerAndTimeWaited`: an orchestrator step waiting on `approval` since 90 minutes before `NOW` shows `[?]`, `wait:approval` and `waited 1h30m`.
- `test_Wait_StepJson_WaitingSinceIsTheFirstWaitEvent`: a wait at minute 1, repeated at minute 5, keeps `waiting_since` at minute 1. A `--phase start` clears it to `""`. A switch from `owner` to `approval` restarts it.
- `test_Wait_ListText_ShowsHowLongTheStepHasWaited`: with the clock patched to 2 hours after the wait began, the step line reads `wait:owner 2h00m`.
- `test_Wait_StepFromDictWithoutWaitingSince_ReadsEmpty`: `Step.from_dict` of a dict without the key gives `""`.
- `test_Counts_Roles_CountStepsUnderTheOrchestrator`: an orchestrator step, plus implementer, ui, reviewer and gate steps with `--parent` set to it, give `roles` `{"orchestrator": 1, "implementer": 1, "ui": 1, "reviewer": 1, "gate": 1}`. A subagent of the implementer is not in `roles`, and `subagents` still counts every step with a parent. The existing `test_Counts_Roles_CountOnlyTopLevelSteps` stays green unchanged.
- `test_Snapshot_Runs_StepsCarryWaitingOnAndQuestion`: a step waiting on an asked question carries `waiting_on` `owner` and the same `question` object as `relay-run list --json`. A running step carries `""` and `null`. Update `test_Snapshot_Runs_OnlyActive`'s expected step dict for the two new keys.
- `test_AnswerGet_MultiLineTextAndWhy_PrintsEveryLine`: after `answer --text "a\nb" --why "c\nd"`, `answer --get` prints `a\nb\nwhy: c\nd\n`, and `--json` keeps both newlines.
- `test_Relay_Heartbeat_SaysItEndsAWait`: `ai.relay_text()` and `ai.orchestrator_text()`, whitespace-normalized, each contain "A heartbeat on a waiting step ends its wait".

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests and watch them go red.
2. Make the `relayrun` changes: `waiting_since`, `in_lane`, `counts`, and the move of `elapsed_text`. Then the TUI marker and row cells, the `list` text, the snapshot keys, and the contract sentence.
3. Update the docs and CHANGELOG. In the closing note, record that the spec-check bullet needed no change and cite `test_Relay_UiPassAndSpecCheckNameTheirLedgerRoles`. Tell ork, in a note on this slice for its next sync, that `counts.roles` changed meaning.
4. Mutation-check each new test.

Size: S at the upper edge. Each change is small, but they touch `relayrun`, `tui`, `cli`, `snapshot` and `ai`. The TUI marker and row cells are the largest piece. If the owner wants a smaller slice, the contract sentence can move to s424.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, then the full suite. `slicer check` passes.
- `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer ai relay | grep -n heartbeat` shows the new sentence.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch; the owner lands it.
